title: Word phrases and nominal sentence: order and agreement

blocks.text: With the module B1.2 from the word to the sentence. The first question is simple only in appearance: in what order are subject and verb put, and how do they agree? In Arabic the answer changes according to order: ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ The ministers have arrived, and the verb to the singular, ⁧الوُزَرَاءُ وَصَلُوا⁩ has the verb in plural. Newspapers write headlines under the first name ( ⁧الحُكُومَةُ تَرْفَعُ الأُجُورَ⁩ ) and the text with the verb before ( ⁧رَفَعَتِ الحُكُومَةُ الأُجُورَ⁩ ). And the plurals of things want the singular feminine: ⁧السَّيَّارَاتُ وَصَلَتْ⁩ . In this unit you put in order all these rules, which you met to pieces in A1 and A2. Two weeks.

The verbal sentence begins with the verb: verb + subject ( ⁧فَاعِل⁩ ) + complements. It is the normal order of narrative and chronicle. The nominal sentence begins with a name, the term "theme" ( ⁧مُبْتَدَأ⁩ ), followed by what is said about it, the "predicate" ( ⁧خَبَر⁩ ). The predicate may be an adjective, a name, a preposition with its complement, or a verbal sentence: ⁧الحُكُومَةُ رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ⁩ = theme ⁧الحُكُومَةُ⁩ + predicate ⁧رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ.⁩ What's the difference? The content is the same; It changes the focus. The nominal sentence highlights the subject (as far as the government is concerned, increased wages) or contrasts it with another. In the spoken language and dialects the SVO order is much more frequent than in the fuṣḥā written.

chapters.title: 3. The agreement in the verbal sentence (verb first)

blocks.text: Rule: the verb before the subject remains to the singular, but it accords in the genre.

Two cases to be recognized. 1. If there are other words between the verb and the female subject, the verb may remain to the male: ⁧حَضَرَ الاِجْتِمَاعَ ثَلَاثُ مُوَظَّفَاتٍ⁩ Three staff members attended the meeting (but ⁧حَضَرَتْ⁩ is always correct). 2. With a plural over people, in the literary language the verb sometimes goes to female: ⁧قَالَتِ الأَعْرَابُ⁩ . In the newspapers you will almost always find the male: ⁧قَالَ الخُبَرَاءُ.⁩ The pronoun subject is inside the verb and does not repeat: ⁧وَصَلُوا⁩ They're here. When the subject has already been appointed, the verb takes the desinence of person: ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ وَعَقَدُوا اجْتِمَاعًا⁩ The Ministers arrived and held a meeting.

chapters.title: 4. The agreement in the nominal sentence (verb after)

blocks.text: Rule: the verb after the subject agrees in everything: gender and number.
dual ⁧الوَزِيرَتَانِ وَصَلَتَا.⁩ · ⁧الوَزِيرَانِ وَصَلَا.⁩ The two ministers/the two minions have arrived.
The same applies to the preaching adjectives: ⁧الطُّلَّابُ مُتْعَبُونَ⁩ , ⁧الطَّالِبَاتُ مُتْعَبَاتٌ.⁩

chapters.title: 7. The Indeterminate Subject: The Predicate Before

blocks.text: A nominal sentence does not normally start with an indefinite name. If the subject is indeterminate, the predicate (a preposition with its complement, a place adverb) goes ahead:

rows: There's a man in the office waiting for you.
There's a car in front of the house.

blocks.text: ⁧هُنَاكَ حَلٌّ آخَرُ.⁩ There is another solution.

Determined or indefinite? With the determined subject the normal order is theme + predicate: ⁧الرَّجُلُ فِي المَكْتَبِ⁩ The man is in the office. With the undetermined entity: ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ رَجُلٌ⁩ There's a man in the office. In Italian, the difference often corresponds to "è" / "c'è" is ".
